editorial.meta_description: The ITIL 4 Specialist HVIT certification is scheduled for retirement on 2027-12-31, and candidates should transition to the ITIL (Version 5) modules for future
editorial.overview: The ITIL 4 Specialist: High Velocity IT (HVIT) exam, certified by PeopleCert (AXELOS), focuses on the digital product lifecycle and the high-velocity nature of modern organizations. It covers four distinct domains, including approaches, models, and safety culture. This linear, 40-question exam is part of the ITIL 4 framework, though it is currently scheduled for retirement on 2027-12-31, with ITIL (Version 5) modules serving as the official successor path for all current and future certification candidates.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is intended for IT professionals managing digital products and services. It is particularly suitable for those working in high-velocity environments who need to understand technical practices, safety culture, and the digital product lifecycle. Candidates should have experience with ITIL 4 concepts before attempting this certification.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official PeopleCert (AXELOS) study documentation to master the four domains. Since this is a 40-question linear exam, practice applying concepts to real-world scenarios. You have 90 minutes to complete the test, so focus on time management. Ensure you are prepared for the 70 percent passing score requirement. As the exam retires on 2027-12-31, prioritize your studies or consider the ITIL (Version 5) modules as your next step.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain examines the high-velocity nature of digital organizations. It focuses on how digital transformation influences service management and the speed at which modern businesses must operate to remain competitive in the digital era.

This domain covers various HVIT approaches and models. It provides the framework for understanding how different methodologies support high-velocity IT and how these models integrate into existing service management structures for better organizational performance.

This domain addresses safety culture and technical practices. It explores how to maintain operational reliability and security while increasing the velocity of IT service delivery through specific technical and cultural implementations within the enterprise.

This domain details the digital product lifecycle. It tracks the progression of digital products from conception to retirement, emphasizing the management of value streams and product-based service delivery to ensure continuous value for customers.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive prepared for a 90-minute session consisting of 40 multiple-choice questions. You must achieve a 70 percent passing score to earn the certification. Manage your time carefully across all four domains to ensure you answer every question before the timer expires.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The exam consists of 40 multiple-choice questions in a linear format. You must answer these questions within the allotted time to demonstrate your proficiency in the subject matter and successfully earn the certification before the retirement date.

To pass the exam and earn your certification, you must achieve a score of 70 percent. This requirement ensures that all candidates have a sufficient understanding of the high-velocity IT concepts covered in the official study documentation.

The exam duration is 90 minutes. During this time, you are expected to complete all 40 questions. It is important to manage your time effectively to ensure you have enough time to review your answers before submitting the exam.

faq.question_title: What is the cost of the exam?
faq.answer_text: The exam price is 430 dollars. This fee covers the cost of the certification attempt. Please ensure you are fully prepared for the exam before scheduling, as the certification is scheduled for retirement on 2027-12-31.

methodology.summary: This editorial was constructed by synthesizing verified facts from PeopleCert (AXELOS) documentation and official exam guides to provide a clear overview of the certification and its retirement path, ensuring all information remains accurate and current for candidates.
